proposals.title: Escape versus recycling: the fate of AGN-driven multiphase outflows
proposals.hypothesis: A substantial fraction of AGN-driven outflowing gas remains gravitationally bound and recycles through the circumgalactic medium, limiting the permanence of feedback-driven gas removal.

prior_evidence.statement: Quasar observations show AGN feedback acting on molecular gas reservoirs at high redshift, but such detections do not determine whether gas escapes the halo.

links.label: quasar molecular-gas reservoirs
links.title: AGN feedback on molecular gas reservoirs in quasars at z~2.4

prior_evidence.statement: Stellar-feedback work on baryon deficiency in low-mass galaxies provides a boundary condition for non-AGN removal channels that must not be confused with AGN-driven escape.

links.label: stellar feedback and baryon deficiency
links.title: Stellar feedback drives the baryon deficiency in low-mass galaxies

prior_evidence.statement: Simulated galaxy feedback constraints highlight that gas removal, recycling, and observable baryon fractions depend on halo scale.

links.label: simulated observable feedback constraints
links.title: Galaxies in a simulated ΛCDM universe II: observable properties and constraints on feedback

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: The escaped fraction of multiphase outflows is unmeasured across a representative mass/redshift sample; an outflow detection is not equivalent to permanent quenching.
proposals.data_plan: AGN hosts and inactive controls spanning stellar mass and redshift; MUSE/MaNGA ionized-gas kinematics, ALMA CO and [C II] for cold gas, JWST/NIRSpec for z>2 outflow tracers, and CGM absorption where available to track recycling.
proposals.decision_criterion: Compare outflow velocity distributions with halo escape velocities inferred from dynamical/halo-mass estimates, then model escaped versus bound/recycling fractions as a function of stellar mass, halo mass, and redshift. A high escaped fraction at fixed denominator supports permanent-removal feedback; a low escaped fraction supports recycling-limited regulation.
proposals.limitations: Projection, phase conversion, and uncertain halo potentials can dominate the escaped-fraction error budget.

proposals.title: Environmental dependence of radio-jet coupling efficiency in galaxy gas
proposals.hypothesis: The fraction of radio-jet mechanical power deposited into the multiphase interstellar or circumgalactic medium varies systematically with ambient gas density and host environment.

prior_evidence.statement: Young radio galaxies show AGN-driven outflows and provide an empirical route to estimating feedback efficiency.

links.label: young radio galaxies and feedback efficiency
links.title: AGN-driven outflows and feedback efficiency in young radio galaxies

prior_evidence.statement: Local M51-scale NOEMA data show how jet/AGN activity can affect molecular ISM structure at high spatial resolution, motivating a broader population test.

links.label: SWAN IV molecular ISM feedback
links.title: SWAN IV: Extent of AGN feedback on the interstellar medium in M51

prior_evidence.statement: Galaxy-group feedback studies identify the group regime as a strong testbed for coupling between radio activity and hot gas.

links.label: group-scale AGN feedback
links.title: Galaxy groups as the ultimate probe of AGN feedback

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: Radio luminosity is not a direct coupling-efficiency measurement; the key unknown is the distribution of deposited energy relative to jet power across host gas conditions.
proposals.data_plan: VLA/LOFAR/MeerKAT for jet morphology and radio spectral ages; Chandra for cavities/shocks/hot gas; MUSE/MaNGA for ionized-gas shock diagnostics; ALMA CO for molecular disturbances; environment from group catalogues.
proposals.decision_criterion: Estimate jet power and gas work/thermal response in the same apertures, then regress coupling efficiency on gas density, environment, and jet age. A robust environmental dependence requires efficiency differences larger than radio-power calibration uncertainties.
proposals.limitations: Radio-to-jet-power conversions are uncertain; coupling estimates must be reported with systematic floors.

proposals.title: Locating the transition from stellar-feedback to AGN-feedback regulation
proposals.hypothesis: There is a stellar/halo-mass regime where stellar-feedback momentum and energy budgets cease to explain gas loss or quiescence, and AGN-linked observables become necessary to reproduce the measured quenched fraction and baryon deficit.

prior_evidence.statement: Low-mass baryon deficiency attributed to stellar feedback provides the low-mass endpoint of the transition problem.

links.label: stellar-feedback baryon deficiency
links.title: Stellar feedback drives the baryon deficiency in low-mass galaxies

prior_evidence.statement: High-redshift environmental-quenching simulations emphasize that quenching mechanisms vary with mass and redshift, not only with local observables.

links.label: high-redshift environmental quenching simulations
links.title: Environmental quenching of high-redshift galaxies: interpreting JWST observations with simulations

prior_evidence.statement: Simulated observable-property constraints show why feedback-regime boundaries must be tested against measured baryonic properties.

links.label: feedback constraints in simulated galaxies
links.title: Galaxies in a simulated ΛCDM universe II: observable properties and constraints on feedback

proposals.remaining_uncertainty: The observational crossover mass between stellar-feedback-dominated regulation and AGN-linked regulation is not cleanly measured with the same denominator and gas observables.
proposals.data_plan: DESI/GAMA/COSMOS parent samples with stellar mass and halo proxy; ALFALFA/FASHI HI and ALMA CO gas fractions; optical/IR SFRs; X-ray/radio AGN indicators; JWST for high-redshift extension.
proposals.decision_criterion: Fit a broken-slope or transition model for gas fraction, baryon deficit, and quenched fraction as functions of stellar/halo mass while including AGN incidence and stellar-feedback proxies. The transition is credible only if the AGN-linked term improves predictive power above the stellar-feedback model at high mass.
proposals.limitations: Halo-mass uncertainties and selection functions can smear the transition; results should be framed as a probability surface, not a single universal mass.

title: Galaxy Evolution — Research proposals on outflows and feedback regimes
reader_facing_summary: This page presents three proposal-style research programmes on outflow fate, jet coupling, and the transition from stellar-feedback to AGN-linked regulation. The proposals are framed around measurable observables, matched denominators, and explicit decision criteria.
